title.en: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) vs Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
title.hi: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) vs Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)

rows.en: Liquid assets (Gold, Cash, G-Secs) held by banks
rows.hi: Liquid assets (Gold, Cash, G-Secs) held by banks

rows.en: Both are quantitative instruments used by RBI to regulate credit creation.
rows.hi: Both are quantitative instruments used by RBI to regulate credit creation.

steps.en: Pre-1991: High CRR levels used for fiscal deficit monetization
steps.hi: Pre-1991: High CRR levels used for fiscal deficit monetization

steps.en: Post-1991: Gradual reduction of CRR to improve banking efficiency
steps.hi: Post-1991: Gradual reduction of CRR to improve banking efficiency

clarification.en: CRR is a reserve requirement on deposits, while Repo Rate is the cost of borrowing funds from RBI.
clarification.hi: CRR is a reserve requirement on deposits, while Repo Rate is the cost of borrowing funds from RBI.

relationship.en: Higher CRR reduces the money multiplier effect in the economy.
relationship.hi: Higher CRR reduces the money multiplier effect in the economy.
